text:
maria: FYI - saw a sharp latency spike on tail tokens for long-context runs (prod model v3). 95th jumped from ~120ms -> 520ms for a burst of requests around 03:12 UTC. Suspect KV reclaim/paging thrash when contexts exceed ~64k tokens. Posting quick notes and a tiny profile snippet.

luca: can you paste the timeline + which eviction policy was active? LRU or FIFO on that pool?

maria: pool=dedicated-gpu-42, policy=FIFO (we had been dogfooding FIFO for a while on that hardware). Timeline:
```
03:11:58 - normal p50/p95
03:12:02 - incoming long ctx batch (30 reqs, avg seq_len 52k)
03:12:02 - KV pages start evicting to make room
03:12:03 - repeated reinserts observed, latency climbs
03:12:12 - traffic drops, slow recovery ~20s
```

priya: interesting. do you see repeated reinsert chains in the logs or just higher page fault counters?

maria: both. snippet from runtime trace (simplified):
```
[evict] shard=3 victim_bucket=0x1f
[reinsert] shard=7 key=0xabc... reinserted->moved to tail
[evict] shard=3 victim_bucket=0x2a
[reinsert] shard=3 key=0xdef... reinserted->tail
[page_out] bytes=12MB
[page_in] bytes=12MB
```
There are back-and-forths where FIFO picks older slots and then we reinsert the same keys shortly after because long contexts touch prefixes. That means cache oscillation.

dan: that aligns with a synthetic I ran earlier: FIFO + sequential long contexts => churn. LRU tends to keep reused prefixes but at cost of more bookkeeping. Do we have perf counters for KV lookup vs reinsert overhead?

maria: yes: reinsert_count spiked to ~14k during the 10s window, lookup hit-rate dropped from 86% -> 47%. CPU hot function was `kv_reinsert_chain` in the runtime. Flamegraph clipped: ~27% of CPU in reinsert path during the surge.

luca: hmm. two axes: correctness (are reinserts safe?) and latency amplification (reinserts blocking request thread). Are reinserts synchronous on request path?

maria: currently reinserts may do small sync updates to bucket lists under per-shard locks. We kept it simple for correctness; that appears to amplify latency under pressure.

priya: I'd advocate for these mitigations (quick list):
- make reinsert async when triggered by requests (queue and batch process)
- add hysteresis to FIFO selectable watermark (avoid immediate eviction after X% usage)
- try LRU hybrid (small LRU window for hot prefixes + FIFO for cold)

dan: +1 for async reinsert. We tried batching reinserts off the hot path in a test harness and 95th dropped ~2.3x. But we saw memory spike because queued reinserts ballooned. Need bounded queue and backpressure.

maria: ran a short A/B in staging: FIFO baseline vs FIFO+async_reinsert (bounded 1024 queue). Results: p95 520ms -> 210ms, p50 unaffected. But under sustained heavy long-ctx traffic queue fills and we start stalling producers -> need fallbacks.

infra-bot: deploy-ci: staging rollout completed for canary=runtime-kv-async-2026-03-17. Logs: canary accepted 1.2k reqs/min, no OOMs.

luca: great. For correctness, ensure ordering semantics preserved: reinserts must not violate KV visibility for concurrent requests. Maria, can you paste the minimal invariants we need?

maria: invariants: 1) a lookup must never miss a key if it was already inserted for that request session; 2) reinserts must preserve latest pointer per shard; 3) async queue must flush before we drop shard metadata on resize. We can implement atomic pointer swaps to keep visibility while doing async fixes.

priya: another angle: kernel selection + batching heuristics. If kernel chooses a path optimized for short sequence lengths but we suddenly feed many long sequences, KV pressure + suboptimal kernel can amplify latency because more time per token + reinserts. We should detect sequence-length distribution shift and pick more conservative kernel/batching so we avoid batch sizes that encourage evictions.

dan: agree. We can add a small runtime probe that computes running median sequence length per pool every 5s and flip kernel/batch heuristics if median > 32k. Low-risk toggles.

maria: action items I tracked:
- (maria) add async bounded reinsert queue + atomic pointer swaps (WIP)
- (luca) instrument per-shard reinsert latency + queue depth dashboards (ETA today)
- (priya) implement seq-len probe and kernel/batch toggle prototype (ETA 48h)
- (dan) test hybrid LRU window in perf harness and repo stress tests (ETA 72h)

luca: also let's add a quick smoke test that synthesizes interleaved long contexts to reproduce. example: 30 concurrent requests with seq_len randomly between 40k-70k, prefix reuse probability 0.6. Run for 60s. I'll add to infra perf suite.

maria: thanks. I'll post the tiny perf flame and the p95 time series after I patch the async reinsert PR.

priya: :thumbsup: keep the PRs small and link to canary metrics. If async queue helps, we can consider making FIFO default but with async reinserts and LRU micro-window fallback.

dan: one caveat: async adds complexity for Private installs with small memory budgets. We must make the bounded queue configurable per-deployment.

maria: agreed. config knobs: queue_size, reinsert_batch_size, seq_len_probe_enabled, policy_hysteresis_pct. I'll include them.

infra-bot: note: opened ticket INF-8272 to track KV-reinsert async rollout and dashboards.

priya: cool. tagging @sre for postmortem if we see another spike.

maria: thanks all, will update thread with PR link + canary metrics.
